newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares set high, seen up on Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares set high, seen up on Wednesday.

text.p: Polish shares set a new 30-month high and analysts said higher turnover and stronger buying after price-fixing signalled another rise on Wednesday, with Warsaw gains linked with recent bourse rises abroad.
"I think the rise here is linked with the bull market on many bourses abroad," said Pawel Tarnowski, an analyst at Raiffeisen Capital and Investment.
Some analysts said the significant supply accompanying the stronger buying after price-fixing on Tuesday signalled only slight growth on Wednesday and a quick slowing of the uptrend.
"Not everybody believes yet that the recent high will be significantly pierced and there'll be a growth trend," said Bogdan Kornacki of Wielkopolski Bank Kredytowy (WBK) brokerage.
The main market's all-share WIG index rose 1.2 percent to 14,993.0 and turnover rose 5.9 percent to 140.3 million zlotys on both markets.

Analysts said the treasury's transfer of 32.9 percent of PBR shares to state-owned Powszechny Bank Kredytowy SA announced after the market closed could have a neutral-to-negative effect on PBR since many had hoped a foreign bank would get the stake.
Analysts were surprised by the scale of top-gainer Relpol's 9.8-percent jump in active trade.
Continuous trade turnover was at 2.2 million zlotys with biggest mover BIG up 2.4 percent.
NFI units slipped 0.3 percent in 17.1-million- zloty continuous trade and were flat at 160 zlotys in the regular bourse session in a turnover of 30.1 million zlotys.
Analysts said profit-taking on the units after their 11.9-percent surge since late September could result in their fall on Wednesday.
